label: rem:ilp-solution-count-unwrap
title: ILP solution count determines unwrap depth via confinement level
html:
Remark. The number of distinct ILP solutions at a given confinement level dictates the unwrap depth required to uniquely specify an atom-knot's normal form.

Let K be an atom at substrate parameter q with normal form currently expressed at level \ell. Let N_\ell(K, q) be the number of integer solutions x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^M to the Frobenius positivity ILP \mathrm{G}(q)\, x \geq 0 within the confinement filtration J^\ell(q).

The unwrap depth at level \ell is:

  d_\ell(K, q) = \max\bigl(0, N_\ell(K, q) - 1\bigr).

Interpretation:

  • N_\ell = 0: unstable at level \ell. The atom cannot exist in this shorthand. It must decay or fully unwrap.
  • N_\ell = 1: uniquely determined at level \ell. The shorthand suffices; no unwrap is needed.
  • N_\ell = k \geq 2: (k-1)-fold ambiguous at level \ell. One must unwrap k-1 levels to disambiguate via finer normal form structure.

Connection to confinement levels. Each unwrap step expands a shorthand word at level \ell into its normal form at level \ell - 1. The finer level accesses a larger filtration J^{\ell-1}(q) \supsetneq J^\ell(q). This richer operator basis distinguishes previously tied ILP solutions. When a coarse effective description exhibits multiple solutions, zooming to the next-finer scale resolves the ambiguity via operator content.

Computational benefit. Non-magic atoms typically exhibit N_\ell = 1 at the coarsest useful level. A single inter-nucleon configuration suffices. Magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 2 at the nucleon level. Shell closure permits multiple equivalent assemblies of the closed shell. Each corresponds to a distinct normal form at the quark level. Double-magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 3 because both proton and neutron closures contribute degeneracy.

Formal statement. Let K be an atom-knot. Then:

  \boxed{\; \text{NF-depth}(K, q) = \text{coarsest level } \ell \text{ with } N_\ell(K, q) = 1 \;}

Computing the normal form at exactly this depth fully specifies the atom's categorical structure. Deeper computation is redundant; shallower computation leaves ambiguity.

Example (proton gluon derivation). The proton's 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) admits N_\ell = 84 feasible ILP solutions at the baryon level. Minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M| selects the unique \sigma_0 \to \sigma_0 solution. If a tie occurs, the framework demands unwrapping to the quark level, where the ILP separates them.

Computational shortcut. Adaptive unwrap reduces cost: storage and Gröbner reduction scale with n_{\text{strands}}^{\text{used}} rather than uniformly with 3A.
